title: December, 2011
logline: Does Chloe come home. A Christmas card, printed, a photo: Chloe and a gray coat with a face this time. Wood pins it photo-in.

panels.composition: The mailbox. A card, glossy. WOOD opening it in the alley.

image.prompt: a man opening a glossy printed holiday card at a mailbox in a gravel alley, an old dog under his arm, December, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: The card: a printed photo. CHLOE, thirty-one, hair pinned, and beside her a man — pleasant, well-dressed, a good coat. Printed text: HAPPY HOLIDAYS FROM CHLOE & JULIAN. The strip draws the man's face for the first time and gives it nothing.

image.prompt: a glossy printed holiday card with a photo of a woman with pinned dark hair beside a pleasant well-dressed man in a good coat, printed text beneath
image.notes: Julian's face, first and nearly only time: pleasant, unremarkable, drawn with deliberate neutrality. HAPPY HOLIDAYS FROM CHLOE & JULIAN. Letter after.

panels.composition: Wood, to the dog, looking at the card a long time.

balloons.text: He looks nice. That's the worst thing I've ever said about anyone.

image.prompt: a man looking at a holiday card for a long moment and speaking quietly to an old dog

panels.composition: The corkboard. Wood pinning the card photo-side to the wall, printed text out. The only card on the board pinned backwards on purpose.

image.prompt: a man pinning a holiday card to a crowded corkboard with its photo turned to the wall so only the printed back shows, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: She doesn't come home. Julian gets a face and it's nice. The card goes up backwards.
